compiled_state.description:
## Observation

The store event write path bounds every lock-held git child (`git add`, `git commit`, `git rm`, `checkout`, `reset`, plus the recovery reads `diff`, `ls-files`, `read-tree`) at 30 s: `event_commit_git._run_git` passes `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 30` to `gitutil.run_git_bounded`. `tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py` pins `event_append._GIT_TIMEOUT == push._GIT_TIMEOUT`.

On 2026-10-27 at ~18:40 PDT a local `rebar edit` on the main checkout's tracker failed with `git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s` (recorded on bug `affordable-omphacite-sunfish`). That tracker measured 213,713 index entries; with its stat cache invalidated, every index-refreshing git command cost ~49 s (`git status --porcelain`). `git commit` and `git add` refresh the index, so their cost grows with index entries, not with the network.

A timeout is not retried: `run_git_bounded` folds it into rc 124 with `git timed out after <n>s`, which neither `_with_index_lock_retry` nor `_with_transient_fault_retry` classifies as retryable. One slow commit therefore fails the write, and the user must redo it.

## Decision (settled from precedent)

- c2ba (`melting-resting-serpent`) existed to make lock-held git calls bounded at all, so a shutdown worst case could be computed. Its record asks for the lock-held calls to carry a timeout "matching `push.py`"; it gives no sizing for index work. The 30 s value was a parity choice with the network push bound.
- The same trade-off was ruled on for sync in `painted-epidermal-shelduck` (Gerrit 3248, `225f227c3fb`): index-heavy local git operations use gitutil's existing 120 s `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`; network operations keep 30 s. `gitutil.run_git_write` already uses 120 s.
- Rule applied here: local index operations in `event_commit_git` use `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (reused, no new constant). Every `_run_git` call on this path is local. Network git (push, fetch) is untouched and keeps 30 s.
- Cost accepted: a stalled volume now holds the store write lock up to 120 s per git call instead of 30 s before the write fails and releases it. This is the same bound `run_git_write` and sync already hold the lock for.

## Approach

1. `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py`: set `_GIT_TIMEOUT = _LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`, keeping the name so `event_append`'s re-export and `review_bot.config.shutdown_force_exit_grace_seconds` follow it. Rewrite its comment to record this decision and both precedents.
2. `tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py`: replace the parity pin with the new relationship: the event-write bound equals `gitutil._LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` and exceeds the network bound, and `push._GIT_TIMEOUT` stays equal to `sync._GIT_TIMEOUT` (network unchanged).
3. Reproduction and regression test in the same file: a `git` wrapper on `PATH` (a `perl` process that sleeps then `exec`s the real git, so the timed-out child is the sleeper itself and nothing is orphaned) stalls `git commit` on the test tracker by the measured 49 s refresh scaled 1/30, about 1.7 s. The module bound is scaled by the same 1/30. At the old 30 s bound (1.0 s scaled) `stage_and_commit` loses the write; at the local bound (4.0 s scaled) the write commits.
4. `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`: re-derive the review-bot `stop_grace_period`. The force-exit deadline is drain 1200 + cancel 10 + lock acquisition 60 + one lock-held git call. At 30 s that was 1300 s, under 1320 s. At 120 s it is 1390 s, past 1320 s, so `test_force_exit_deadline_stays_within_the_stop_grace_band` fails until compose follows. New value: 1390 + the 45 s push-reconcile lock term from the existing derivation = 1435 s, rounded up to a whole 24 minutes = 1440 s, with the arithmetic in the comment. MCP's 1260 s derives only from `_mcp_health.DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` (1200 s) and does not change.

**Out of scope:** push/fetch bounds and retry policy; the external copied-worktree cause of the stat-dirty index (`affordable-omphacite-sunfish`).

## Testing

- New test fails before the fix (the write is lost at the scaled 30 s bound) and passes after.
- Updated c2ba pin test, existing c2ba wiring tests, the review-bot stop-grace tests, and the store write/concurrency modules pass.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, then `make verify`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The c2ba record is read and confirms its 30 s bound was set for parity with push, not sized for index work; the decision and both precedents are recorded on this ticket and in the `_GIT_TIMEOUT` comment in `event_commit_git.py`.
- [x] Local index operations on the event write path are bounded by `gitutil._LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`, with no new constant; network git operations keep the 30 s push bound.
- [x] The c2ba pin test asserts the new relationship (event-write bound == local bound > network bound; push bound unchanged).
- [x] A slow-index regression test reproduces the lost write at the scaled old bound and shows the write committing at the scaled local bound.
- [x] The review-bot `stop_grace_period` is re-derived from the new worst case and updated, with the arithmetic in a comment; the MCP grace is confirmed independent of this bound.
- [x] Every `src/rebar` file stays at or under 800 lines, and the complexity ratchet reports no new or increased function.
- [x] `make verify` exits 0.
